question.worked_solution:
First, notice that the $1$st row of our determinant is almost equal to the $2$nd row. So, we can rewrite the given determinant, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}300 & 250 & 100 \\ 300 & 270 & 100 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}| & =|\begin{aligned}300 & 250 & 100 \\ 300+0 & 250+20 & 100+0 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

Next, using the linearity property of determinants, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}300 & 250 & 100 \\ 300+0 & 250+20 & 100+0 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}| & =|\begin{aligned}300 & 250 & 100 \\ 300 & 250 & 100 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}|+|\begin{aligned}300 & 250 & 100 \\ 0 & 20 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

The first determinant must be zero since it has two identical rows, while the second determinant can be expanded across the $2$nd row, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}300 & 250 & 100 \\ 300 & 250 & 100 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}|+|\begin{aligned}300 & 250 & 100 \\ 0 & 20 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}| & =0+20(-1)^{2+2}|\begin{aligned}300 & 100 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =20\cdot (300\cdot 1-100\cdot 1) \\  & =20\cdot 200 \\  & =4\,000\end{aligned}
$$
